messages.author: 80defc9c4046a73b
messages.subject: Suggestions on debugging hosted apps.
parts:
Hi. I have an app that runs on 8100 on my local machine, but when I upload it to spark, it freezes (one specific menu grays out and the apps stops responding). I got it narrowed down to a specific line that sets a value in a reactiveValues object. Unfortunately, this flag is what triggers the rendering of most of the other menus.

The appropriate file in my ~/ShinyApps/log/ directory show a normal launch followed by a termination (that would be me typing killall R). When I set options(shiny.trace=T), I get the expected spools of output, but still nothing incriminating.

What should I try next to get to the bottom of this? Ordinarily I would keep put in "cat(...)" statements, dump environments to scratch files and read them from a separate session, and keep poking around until I eventually found it. But the lag will make this a much more lengthy and painfull process than on a local machine. I'm hoping someone can save me some time with suggestions on where to look. Or if perhaps there is somehow a way to get into "browser()" even on a hosted app? Or some way to force it to emit an error message instead of failing silently or (more likely, given the grayed-out behavior of the affected widget) getting into some endless loop somewhere?

By the way, there are no warning or error messages when the same code executes on my local machine.

Or, has there been a change between 0.7.X and 0.4.X that specifically affects setting a value inside a reactiveValues object (from within a renderUI command block, if that matters)? My localhost runs 0.4.1.99 and spark runs 0.7.0.

Thanks.

messages.author: 80defc9c4046a73b
messages.subject: Re: Suggestions on debugging hosted apps.
parts:
Thank you. I upgraded to 0.7.0 and was able to replicate the problem locally. I apologize for what in hindsight was a lazy question, despite my disclaimers.

It appears that what's different in 0.7.0 is that now writing to a value inside a reactiveValues object causes an endless loop if it's done in a scope that is invalidated by a _different_ value inside the same reactiveValues object. In other words, in 0.4.x it was okay to have a statement like "revals$foo <- 1" in the same enclosure as "bar <- revals$bar" but in 0.7.0 an endless loop results (and it's silent even with "options(shiny.trace=T)", you have to manually cat some sort of message from inside the function in order to see what's wrong).

This can be fixed by wrapping the assignment statement in "isolate()".

Another side note about upgrading shiny that might matter to someone:

I'm running R 2.15.3 on Lucid 10.04.4 LTS. When I tried to "install.packages('shiny')" it failed on compiling the "httpuv" package. When I did "devtools::install_github('httpuv'); devtools::install_github('shiny')" it worked but claimed to install v0.6.0.99. However, when I again tried "install.packages('shiny')", it installed v0.7.0 with no further comments.

parts: > In other words, in 0.4.x it was okay to have a statement like "revals$foo <- 1" in the same enclosure as "bar <- revals$bar" but in 0.7.0 an endless loop results

That doesn't seem right, I tried duplicating this and it only executes once:

library(shiny)
v <- reactiveValues(a=1, b=2)
observe({
  v$a <- 1
  bar <- v$b
  print('executed')
})
shiny:::flushReact()

Are you sure there's not more going on in that reactive scope?
